newsitem.title: POLAND: SOCCER-WIDZEW SEIZE FIRST CHAMPIOMS' LEAGUE POINTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WIDZEW SEIZE FIRST CHAMPIOMS' LEAGUE POINTS.

text.p: Polish side Widzew Lodz won their first points in the European Champions' League on Wednesday with a 2-0 victory over Steaua Bucharest in group B.

Both sides now have only forlorn hopes of stopping Atletico Madrid and Borussia Dortmund from securing the two available qualifying places, but the result was encouraging for a Polish side who have latterly been beset by injuries.
Widzew opened the scoring in the 39th minute through striker Slawomir Majak, who headed Radoslaw Michalski's cross into the net.
The Polish champions sustained that momentum into the second half and in the 49th minute midfielder Ryszard Czerwiec scored with a powerful 18-metre shot.

Widzew had the ball in the net again midway through the second half, but Italian referee Graziano Cesari disallowed it back after Lodz fans threw a second ball on to the field just before Marek Citko's shot went into Steaua's net.
Widzew's coach Franciszek Smuda said the key to the victory had been the return of several key players including play-marker Ryszard Czerwiec, back after a month-long injury.
"It is very difficult to play against tough opponents in the Champions' League with five players missing. These players know each other and play well together," Smuda said.
Steaua's coach Dumitru Dumitriu said that if his team had scored an early goal, the outcome might have been different.
Referee Cesari booked Bucharest's Ilie Miu, Tiberiu Csik and Tudorel Zamfirescu and Widzew's Miroslaw Szymkowiak.
